prompt: Servers ran at 70% CPU with fine latency. Traffic grew 25%, utilization hit 88%, and latency tripled.
why: Queueing delay grows like 1/(1 − utilization): near 90% small increases cause big waits.
trap: Latency isn't linear in load; plan headroom.

prompt: Finance asks why the team won't run the database at 95% CPU to save money.
why: At 95%, any burst queues dramatically. Target ~60–75% for latency-sensitive systems.
trap: Unused capacity looks like waste until you see the latency curve.

prompt: A single build runner is busy 92% of the day, and developers wait 40 minutes for builds that take 5.
tells: wait 40 minutes for builds that take 5
why: Near-full utilization means long queues. A second runner drops utilization and waits sharply.
trap: Making builds faster helps, but adding capacity off the knee helps more.

prompt: Autoscaling triggers at 90% CPU, but by the time new instances boot, latency has already spiked.
why: 90% is already past the knee; scale earlier (around 60–70%) to leave room for boot time.
trap: The autoscaler works; its threshold ignores queueing math.
